key_insight: The paper proposes unifying online RL with verifiable rewards and preference optimization by replacing brittle scalar rewards with a general preference verifier, enabling continuous exploration and alignment for open-ended tasks.
problem_solved: It closes the split between verifier-driven RL (good for programmatic tasks but not open-ended) and preference optimization (good for open-ended generation but lacking continuous exploration), enabling RL-style improvement on open-ended LLM behaviors.
method: Introduce a general preference verifier that judges open-ended quality instead of relying on a single scalar reward model.
Integrate the verifier into an online reinforcement learning loop so models can continuously explore and improve on open-ended tasks.
Train the verifier from preference data (human or synthetic) and use it to produce learning signals for policy updates.
impact: This approach enables practitioners to apply RL-style fine-tuning and exploration to open-ended LLM tasks (creative writing, dialogue, alignment) while keeping preference-based supervision—improving both capability and safety during post-training.
